channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Hamer rejoins Baker McKenzie
item.description: Mark Hamer has stepped down as deputy assistant attorney general in the Department of Justice’s antitrust division and will return to Baker McKenzie.

item.title: Creditor pacts not subject to antitrust, lenders say
item.description: Several of the world’s largest asset managers have argued that a price-fixing suit filed by Altice USA ignores longstanding precedent that creditor agreements on debt refinancing do not violate antitrust law.

item.title: Hamer time: The Tipline for 9 February 2026
item.description: Go with the flow, it is said. Mark Hamer has left the Department of Justice’s antitrust division to return to Baker McKenzie’s antitrust partnership. The former deputy assistant attorney general said in a statement that he was “grateful” for his time and “excited to return home”. To break it down, also in Tipline, California has voted to add merger filing requirements.

item.title: New Zealand: Competition Authority takes bold steps towards an antimonopoly evolution
item.description: The Commerce Commission of New Zealand is reshaping its antimonopoly framework with recent amendments to the Commerce Act, designed to enhance clarity and enforcement against anti-competitive practices. While the authority has initiated investigations into exclusionary conduct, it has yet to tackle cases involving Big Tech or digital markets, opting for a 'wait and see' strategy. item.title: Whizzed through: The Briefing for 10 February 2026
item.description: The EU has approved Google’s largest-ever acquisition, waving through its $32 billion takeover of cloud security platform Wiz after it was filed last month. Competition commissioner Teresa Ribera said today that Google “stands behind” Microsoft and Amazon in terms of market share for cloud infrastructure, and that customers will continue to have credible alternatives to choose from after the deal ...

item.title: Apple seeks novel de-certification of UK iPhone battery claim
item.description: Apple has urged the UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal to strike out an already-certified £853 million opt-out lawsuit against the company, arguing that the claim has since narrowed and potentially falls under consumer protection rules.

item.title: Apple and Google avoid binding DMCC commitments, critics call proposals “lightweight”
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority has secured voluntary commitments from Apple and Google to deliver greater transparency and “fairness” across their mobile ecosystems, but critics say the agreements amount to “lightweight” steps unlikely to “materially shift” competition.

item.title: UK needs consumer protection collective action regime, ex-enforcer says
item.description: “Wedging” consumer claims into competition cases is “breaking" the UK’s class action regime, the former deputy general counsel at the Competition and Markets Authority has warned.

item.title: Justice league: The Tipline for 10 February 2026
item.description: The Department of Justice has taken down a man of steel using the Sherman Act rather than kryptonite. The Antitrust Division and US Department of Defense’s inspector general investigation ended with the president of Gulfstream Steel & Supply pleading guilty to rigging bids submitted to the US military. Also in Tipline, Amazon seeks to dismiss California’s pricing parity case.

item.title: Paramount races for merger clearance, adds to WB offer
item.description: Paramount has said it largely completed the Department of Justice’s second request just two months after launching a $108 billion hostile bid for Warner Bros Discovery.
